t021: Building together from three parts of Brazil.
t034: We are Beatriz, Sonia and Olivia. SheBuilds combines product development, systems analysis and business strategy to turn concrete needs into solutions people can understand and use.
t035: We work remotely from Pernambuco, Brasília and São Paulo. Our agricultural experience predates SafraFlux: Beatriz and Sonia built award-winning projects together and presented RaízesGo at CNPA 2024. Olivia brings experience in innovation, acceleration and business models, as well as connections in agricultural and coffee communities.
t036: We start with coffee: one sale may bring together the work of several families. Our question is simple — how can we connect that receipt to a clear explanation of each producer’s share?
t042: One collective sale. A clear share for each producer.
t043: SafraFlux helps finance teams at coffee cooperatives and small exporters connect receipts to lots, track installments and explain each producer’s share. USDC is the token used in the primary payment-request integration; Solana is the network used to verify those receipts.
t046: Public demo with fictional data. No login or real money.

t059: THE PROBLEM WE CHOSE TO SOLVE
t062: A coffee sale may involve several families, different quantities and quality premiums. Payments may arrive in installments — and the receipt alone does not explain each person’s share.
t065: Producers, lots, payment requests, installments, history and individual statements connected in an accountability workflow.
t068: Access to their own share after the cooperative confirms the relationship. Quantity, base amount, premium and total are visible, with review and correction requests.
t071: An identified payment request with a reference and QR code. Our initial audience already needs a reason to use this payment method.
t074: Two contributions to the same lot.
t075: With deliveries of 60 kg and 40 kg, allocation by quantity produces 600 and 400 USDC. With a 10% premium and quality scores of 2 and 1, the statement becomes 615 and 385 USDC.
t076: Fictional example of the demo rules. Quality is declared by the operation; the blockchain does not certify physical delivery. The calculation does not move funds.

t118: The product’s value lies in its workflow. Integrations help identify and verify payments, with explicit responsibilities.
t121: Solana Pay requests with a reference and QR code. Server verification checks network, token, recipient, reference, amount and finalization using the signature provided by the operator.
t124: Adapters for Base, Arbitrum, Ethereum L1 and HyperEVM with USDC; Tempo with pathUSD and Robinhood Chain with USDG. The commercial association between payment and lot is declared by the operator.
t127: Cloak integrates private USDC flows on Solana. Zcash uses native ZEC and has local regtest evidence. Financial validation of Cloak on mainnet and external wallets remains pending.
t129: Cloudflare Workers supports the application, API and payment verification. Cloudflare D1 stores account-isolated records, revision history and recovery. Google/GitHub and an authenticator provide access.
t131: Beatriz leads and develops the product. OpenAI Codex supported implementation, debugging, tests and documentation; third-party libraries and SDKs are declared in the SafraFlux repository.
t132: SafraFlux does not store wallet private keys or provide bridges, currency conversion or Pix execution. Verifying a transfer does not prove the coffee’s physical quality or the declared commercial association.
t136: We want to learn from the people carrying out finance operations and measure whether the product solves a recurring need.
t139: We plan 14 interviews to understand problem frequency, existing tools and who approves adoption. These are not achieved results yet.
t142: Validate external wallets, funded payments and Cloak on mainnet. Prepare shared organization roles and independent review.
t145: Seek two pilots with a defined scope to compare reconciliation effort, statement comprehension, discrepancies and required support.
t148: The hypothesis is a subscription per organization, with optional onboarding. Demand, pricing and cost to serve need validation; no paying customers or revenue are confirmed.
t150: We seek conversations with coffee cooperatives and small exporters, technical guidance for validation and business mentorship. Contacts and communities are an entry point; they are not confirmed partnerships.
